page: Amazon Web Services r5b.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. The virtual machine allocates 2 vCPUs backed by 1 dedicated physical core with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no local storage, requiring attached network storage volumes, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight entry-level computational capability bounded by the single physical core. PassMark CPU scoring registers at 2004.55, while Geekbench yields 1138.0 for single-core and 1356.0 for multi-core performance. In stress-ng, the system achieves 1273.69 in single-core and 1675.38 in multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth reaches 95.91 GB/sec for small cached reads and 12.97 GB/sec for large uncached reads. Real-world operational throughput demonstrates 1.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.88 GB/sec in static web serving tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high memory density per compute unit without the overhead of higher vCPU allocations. The primary tradeoff is constrained multi-threaded execution due to the dual-thread single-core design. The r5b.large is primarily fitted for small in-memory caches, development databases, lightweight backend services, and test environments where memory footprint exceeds CPU demands.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.large is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. It features 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 1 Gbps baseline network profile. The instance omits local disk storage and GPU hardware, depending on network storage for persistent data. Synthetic benchmarks reflect conservative processing capabilities, registering 1138.0 on single-core and 1356.0 on multi-core Geekbench runs, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 2004.55. Application metrics indicate 1.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.88 GB/sec static web throughput. By providing an 8 GB per vCPU density, the configuration optimizes cost efficiency for memory-sensitive tasks where computational demands remain minimal. The server is suited for lightweight database workloads, staging environments, Redis caching nodes, and small memory-intensive background utilities.
